FAA Pauses Router Installations After Nationwide Ground Stop

Agency approved daytime upgrade to the network in Arkansas and a contractor’s step-by-step installation plan

By

and

The Federal Aviation Administration has halted installations of routers at the center of communications disruptions that prompted a rare, nationwide ground stop.

FAA officials said the pause will be in place while the agency assesses what went wrong Friday—an ordeal that resulted in nearly 20,000 flights being canceled and thousands more delayed—with equipment at its facilities.

“I feel highly confident that we won’t repeat this level of disruption,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said Tuesday at a press conference in Washington, D.C.

On Friday, L3Harris Technologies, the government contractor in charge of running the FAA’s antiquated air-traffic communications network, installed a new router at a radio transmitter site in southern Arkansas. That router appears to have begun spewing out data that swamped the network, leading to interference with communications between pilots and air-traffic controllers around the country, federal officials have said.
